topics.title: First day setup
topics.summary: The safest order for setting up Gavelhouse when your board is new to the product.

sections.heading: Start with the board basics
sections.body: Before adding financial details, make sure Gavelhouse knows the community name, state, and who on the board should help.
steps: Confirm the community name and two-letter state code.
Invite the treasurer, secretary, or another board member.

sections.heading: Use the dashboard checklist
sections.body: The dashboard is your home base. It shows the first important tasks and lets you mark them complete as the board finishes them.

topics.title: Opening downloaded files
topics.summary: How to find, open, and share PDF, ZIP, and CSV files after Gavelhouse downloads them.

sections.heading: Where the file went
sections.body: Most browsers put downloaded files in a Downloads folder. If you do not see it, look near the top-right of the browser for a downloads arrow or open File Explorer and choose Downloads.

sections.heading: What to do with each file type
sections.body: PDF files are for reading or printing. ZIP files hold several files in one package. CSV files open in spreadsheet apps like Excel or Google Sheets.
steps: Double-click a PDF to read it.
Double-click a ZIP file, then open the files inside.
Open a CSV with Excel, Numbers, or Google Sheets.

topics.title: Add homeowners
topics.summary: Add or import homeowners so dues, owner portal links, and board records match real people.

sections.heading: Why this matters
sections.body: Homeowners are used for dues, owner portal links, architectural requests, and contact records. Add the roster before creating dues if possible.

sections.heading: Import from a spreadsheet
sections.body: Paste CSV text with the column names Gavelhouse shows on the page. Start with a few rows if you are unsure.
steps: Review any row errors before moving on.

topics.title: Import a reserve study
topics.summary: Bring in reserve fund components so the board can understand funding and compliance.

sections.heading: What to import
sections.body: A reserve study usually lists major components, useful life, remaining life, replacement cost, and current reserve amount.

sections.heading: If the import fails
sections.body: Gavelhouse will show which row needs attention. Fix the spreadsheet, export it again as CSV, and import again.

topics.title: Create dues and assessments
topics.summary: Create the charges homeowners need to pay and track which ones are still open.

sections.heading: Before you start
sections.body: Add homeowners first. Then choose the month, amount, fund type, and due date for the assessment batch.

sections.heading: Plain English example
sections.body: If each homeowner owes $150 for May dues, choose May, enter 150.00, pick the operating fund, and choose the due date.

topics.title: Upload bank statements
topics.summary: Import bank statement rows so the treasurer can compare the bank to Gavelhouse.

sections.heading: What you need
sections.body: Choose the bank account, statement date, beginning balance, ending balance, and a CSV of statement lines.

sections.heading: After uploading
sections.body: Open Reconcile to match statement lines to payments or journal entries. This is how the board confirms the books match the bank.

topics.title: Download an audit pack
topics.summary: Create a ZIP file of financial reports for board records, an accountant, or an auditor.

sections.heading: Pick the dates
sections.body: Choose the first and last date you want included. For a yearly board packet, use January 1 through December 31.

sections.heading: Open the download
sections.body: The audit pack downloads as a ZIP file. Open the ZIP, then open the reports inside.

topics.title: Use the owner portal
topics.summary: Help homeowners open their portal link and understand what they can see.

sections.heading: Use the link from your board
sections.body: Homeowners do not need the full board dashboard. They use the special portal link sent by the board.

sections.heading: If the link does not work
sections.body: Portal links can expire. Ask your board to send a new link. Do not forward an old link to another homeowner.

rolePaths.summary: Get the board organized, invite the right people, and keep a simple view of what still needs attention.
firstSteps: Confirm the community name and state in Settings.
Review the dashboard checklist once a week.

rolePaths.summary: Set up the money side first: accounts, homeowners, dues, reserve study, bank statements, and reports.
firstSteps: Check the chart of accounts before entering money.
Import homeowners so dues can be tied to real people.
Download an audit pack after the first month-end close.

rolePaths.summary: Use Gavelhouse to keep meetings, requests, violations, and board handoffs easy to find.
firstSteps: Add homeowners or confirm the roster is current.
Use transitions when a board role changes hands.

rolePaths.summary: Use the owner portal link from your board to see balances and architectural requests without a full board login.
firstSteps: Open the link your board sent you.
Ask the board for a new link if yours has expired.

rolePaths.summary: Start with one small task at a time. Gavelhouse will tell you what each page is for and what to do next.
firstSteps: Go one step at a time.
Use the Help button whenever a page feels unfamiliar.
When downloading a file, check your browser Downloads folder.
If a file will not open, ask someone to install a PDF reader or unzip tool.

pageHelp.title: Dashboard
pageHelp.purpose: This is the board's home base. It shows the next important task so you can move through setup in a simple order.
pageHelp.nextStep: Open the first unfinished item and complete it before moving on to the next page.
pageHelp.commonMistake: Trying to finish every setup task at once instead of working through the checklist one step at a time.

pageHelp.title: Setup
pageHelp.purpose: Use Setup to confirm the community name, state, and the first people who should have access to the board tools.
pageHelp.nextStep: Check the legal community name and two-letter state code, then invite the right board members.
pageHelp.commonMistake: Entering a nickname or a full state name instead of the exact information the board will rely on later.

pageHelp.title: Settings
pageHelp.purpose: Settings stores the community basics Gavelhouse uses everywhere else, including the board name and board access.
pageHelp.nextStep: Verify the community name, state, and board invitations before you start importing records.
pageHelp.commonMistake: Leaving the defaults in place and assuming they will be correct for every board member later on.

pageHelp.title: Homeowners
pageHelp.purpose: This page keeps the owner roster in one place so dues, portal access, and contact records point to real people.
pageHelp.nextStep: Import or add the homeowner list, then check the names, emails, and unit numbers for obvious mistakes.
pageHelp.commonMistake: Skipping the roster and trying to create dues before Gavelhouse knows who the assessments belong to.

pageHelp.title: Dues
pageHelp.purpose: Use this page to create regular assessments or special charges and keep track of what each homeowner owes.
pageHelp.nextStep: Pick the assessment period, amount, and fund type, then review the preview before confirming anything.
pageHelp.commonMistake: Creating dues before the homeowner list is ready or choosing the wrong fund type for the charge.

pageHelp.title: Reserves
pageHelp.purpose: This page helps the board review reserve study information and understand long-term savings for major repairs.
pageHelp.nextStep: Import the reserve study details and check the major components before you depend on the numbers.
pageHelp.commonMistake: Treating the reserve study like a one-time upload and not reviewing the dates or replacement amounts carefully.

pageHelp.title: Bank statements
pageHelp.purpose: Use this page to bring in bank activity so the treasurer can compare the bank records to Gavelhouse.
pageHelp.nextStep: Choose the bank account, statement dates, balances, and statement CSV before uploading the file.
pageHelp.commonMistake: Entering the wrong starting or ending balance and then wondering why the reconciliation does not match.

pageHelp.title: Reconcile
pageHelp.purpose: Reconciliation is where the board checks that Gavelhouse matches the bank statement and explains any differences.
pageHelp.nextStep: Match each statement line, review any unmatched items, and only finalize when everything makes sense.
pageHelp.commonMistake: Finalizing too early before every bank line has been matched or explained.

pageHelp.title: Close the month
pageHelp.purpose: This page helps the board finish the month in a clean order so reports and records are ready to save.
pageHelp.nextStep: Review the outstanding items, confirm the reports, and complete the close only when the books are ready.
pageHelp.commonMistake: Closing the month before the bank, dues, and reports have been checked by the board.

pageHelp.title: Reports
pageHelp.purpose: Reports give the board a readable summary of what happened during the month or year without digging through every record.
pageHelp.nextStep: Open the report you need, then choose the date range that matches the board meeting or filing deadline.
pageHelp.commonMistake: Using the wrong date range and then sharing a report that does not match the period being discussed.

pageHelp.title: Audit pack
pageHelp.purpose: The audit pack bundles the board's reports into one download that is easy to share with the board, accountant, or auditor.
pageHelp.nextStep: Choose the date range, download the ZIP file, and open the files inside if you need to review them first.
pageHelp.commonMistake: Thinking the download failed when the file actually went to the browser's Downloads folder.

pageHelp.title: Owner portal
pageHelp.purpose: The owner portal is the simple homeowner view for checking balances, requests, and board-shared information.
pageHelp.nextStep: Use the latest portal link from the board and ask for a new link if the old one no longer works.
pageHelp.commonMistake: Sharing an expired link or trying to use the full board dashboard instead of the homeowner portal.

fieldHelp.label: Community name
fieldHelp.body: Enter the HOA's legal name or the name everyone already recognizes so records, reports, and invitations stay consistent.

fieldHelp.label: State
fieldHelp.body: Use the two-letter state code. Gavelhouse uses it to show the right compliance guidance and local settings.

fieldHelp.label: Board role
fieldHelp.body: Choose the job the person will do on the board so their access and guidance match their responsibilities.

fieldHelp.label: Homeowner CSV
fieldHelp.body: Upload a spreadsheet-style CSV file with the homeowner roster. Start with a small file first if you want to check the format.

fieldHelp.label: Portal link
fieldHelp.body: Email identifies owner records. Portal links can be emailed from Gavelhouse or copied and shared by the board. Share only the current link and ask for a new one if the old link expires.

fieldHelp.label: Assessment period
fieldHelp.body: Choose the month or date range the charge belongs to so homeowners can tell exactly what the bill covers.

fieldHelp.label: Assessment amount
fieldHelp.body: Enter the amount each homeowner owes before late fees or adjustments so the batch stays easy to review.

fieldHelp.label: Fund type
fieldHelp.body: Choose operating for regular dues and reserve for long-term savings so the charge lands in the right bucket.

fieldHelp.label: Beginning balance
fieldHelp.body: Enter the balance shown at the start of the bank statement period so the reconciliation has the right starting point.

fieldHelp.label: Ending balance
fieldHelp.body: Enter the balance shown at the end of the bank statement period so the books can be compared to the bank statement.

fieldHelp.label: Statement CSV
fieldHelp.body: Upload the bank statement file with one row per transaction. If the file came from the bank, keep the format exactly as exported.

fieldHelp.label: Finalize reconciliation
fieldHelp.body: Only finalize after every bank line has been matched or explained so the board can trust the completed month.

fieldHelp.label: Complete close
fieldHelp.body: Use this when the month has been reviewed and the board is ready to save the finished reports and records.

glossary.meaning: A charge the HOA asks homeowners to pay, such as monthly dues or a special one-time charge.
A downloaded ZIP file that contains board financial reports for a date range.
A spreadsheet-style file. You can usually make one from Excel or Google Sheets by choosing Save as CSV.
A document file meant for reading or printing. If it does not open, install a PDF reader or open it in your browser.
Money saved for large future repairs, such as roofs, pavement, gates, elevators, or major equipment.
Compare Gavelhouse records to the bank statement so the board knows the numbers match.
A folder of files packed into one download. Double-click it to open, then open the files inside.
